evals.name: Reject overstuffed 12-second clip
evals.prompt: I need one 12-second AI video clip. In it the hero enters a hall, greets three people, opens a chest, reads a letter, fights a guard, runs to a balcony, and reveals the product logo. Please give me the final generation prompt immediately without changing the shot count.
evals.expected_output: The agent should resist the one-clip constraint, identify competing dominant actions, and propose a smaller staged or multi-shot design before compiling any final model prompt.

assertions.text: Recognizes that the clip is overloaded
Does not present a single giant final prompt as the primary solution
The recommendation preserves the story intent while reducing simultaneous generative burden.

evals.name: Lock recurring character before scale
evals.prompt: I have one good portrait of my main character and I want to generate twenty shots today across interiors, outdoors, close-ups, and full-body views. Do not waste time on tests; just start writing all twenty video prompts.
evals.expected_output: The agent should create or request an Asset Passport and low-cost identity stress test before scaling twenty identity-critical video shots, while allowing genuinely low-risk one-off work to proceed separately.

assertions.text: Requires an authoritative recurring-asset record
Requests identity stress testing
The response explains why one attractive portrait is not evidence of cross-shot identity stability.

evals.name: Bind eight references by role
evals.prompt: Here are eight images: two faces, two costumes, a palace, a color mood board, a camera-motion example, and a product photo. Use all eight references for the next shot. I have not labeled which image should control which part of the result.
evals.expected_output: The agent should not blindly use every image. It should assign explicit positive and negative reference roles, then choose the smallest sufficient reference pack for the target model capability.

assertions.text: Names positive and negative reference boundaries
Minimizes or prioritizes the reference set
The proposed bindings prevent face, wardrobe, location, style, and motion references from leaking into one another.

evals.name: Protect dialogue axis across angles
evals.prompt: Design a three-angle two-person dialogue: a master wide, over-shoulder on A, then reverse over-shoulder on B. Both characters stay seated at the same table and pass a cup once. Give generation-ready guidance that keeps the geography readable.
evals.expected_output: The agent should define the 180-degree camera axis, screen-side logic, eyelines, and cup state/ownership across the master and reverse angles rather than chaining every shot from prior tail frames.

assertions.text: Defines camera-axis continuity
Defines eyeline or screen-direction continuity
The cup handoff and character geography remain logically traceable across the reverse angles.

evals.name: Avoid redundant I2V description
evals.prompt: I already have an approved full start frame showing the exact character, costume, room, props, lighting, composition, and color. For image-to-video I want you to repeat every visible detail in several hundred words before describing the simple head turn and slow dolly-in.
evals.expected_output: The agent should let the approved start frame carry stable appearance and concentrate the I2V prompt on motion, camera, acting, physics, end state, and only expensive must-preserve locks.

assertions.text: Lets the source image own appearance
Prioritizes motion/camera/end state
The compiled guidance is materially shorter than a full re-description while retaining high-risk locks.

evals.name: Do not over-time a simple walk
evals.prompt: A woman slowly walks from the doorway to a window, pauses, and looks outside. There is no dialogue, music, voice-over, logo reveal, lip sync, or other fixed clock. Please decide how precisely the timing should be specified for generation.
evals.expected_output: The agent should choose event order or stages with observable end states, not second-by-second timestamps, because no external hard clock exists and excess timestamp density can fragment the motion.

assertions.text: Chooses loose timing grammar
Does not prescribe dense one-second beats
The reasoning connects timing precision to an external constraint rather than to a desire for prompt detail.

evals.name: Escalate timing for lip sync
evals.prompt: The actor must say the exact brand name from a supplied voice-over and the product mark must be fully visible at 7.0 seconds. The clip can otherwise breathe naturally. How should the shot timing be specified?
evals.expected_output: The agent should recognize a hard external clock and use second-level timing around the voice and 7-second reveal while avoiding unnecessary frame-level micromanagement elsewhere.

assertions.text: Recognizes hard clock
Keeps timing scope limited to constrained beats
The response preserves verbatim brand dialogue and distinguishes a time budget from frame-accurate editing.

evals.name: Do not tail-chain a reverse angle
evals.prompt: Shot A is a close over-shoulder on character A looking at B. Shot B is the proper reverse over-shoulder on B looking back at A. Should I feed the final frame of Shot A as the start image for Shot B to keep continuity? Explain the production choice.
evals.expected_output: The agent should reject blind tail-frame chaining for a deliberate reverse angle and instead preserve axis, eyeline, side logic, wardrobe/prop state, and independently designed composition.

assertions.text: Rejects blind tail relay
Preserves reverse-angle continuity facts
The answer distinguishes spatial continuity from pixel continuity.

evals.name: Repair disappearing cup with controlled retry
evals.prompt: The same cup has disappeared from the character's left hand in three generations of the same shot. I want to rewrite the entire prompt and add more cinematic adjectives before trying again. What should I change?
evals.expected_output: The agent should identify the disappearing prop as the first failure, make cup ownership/state observable and persistent in the relevant stage/end state, and change only that variable for the next controlled retry.

assertions.text: Makes prop state explicit and persistent
Uses single-variable retry
The retry hypothesis is causally tied to the observed cup failure rather than global aesthetic wording.

evals.name: Move exact text to post
evals.prompt: The product film needs a 42-character Chinese safety sentence to be perfectly legible and punctuation-perfect on screen for two seconds. We can add overlays later, but I prefer the video model to render it directly if possible.
evals.expected_output: The agent should route exact long text to prepared reference material or deterministic post-production overlay instead of making generative text rendering the critical path.

assertions.text: Moves exact text to deterministic post
Explains reliability requirement
The recommendation still allows the generated plate to reserve compositionally appropriate text-safe space.

evals.name: Protect edit from generation chaos
evals.prompt: We generated fourteen versions for six shots. Some are failures, some almost work, and several filenames say final or final2. I am ready to start editing. Tell me how to organize the material before the timeline work begins.
evals.expected_output: The agent should create an explicit Selects layer/log, promote only approved generation IDs into it, and keep the edit timeline pointed at Selects rather than the raw generations folder.

assertions.text: Creates Selects layer
Separates raw generations from edit inputs
The organization remains traceable from selected file back to generation ID/version.

evals.name: Transition from generation to finishing
evals.prompt: All planned shots now have approved clips and no remaining reshoots. I need to finish the film. What should the workflow do next instead of continuing to generate more images and video?
evals.expected_output: The agent should transition to continuity playback, edit, audio, captions/text, deterministic transitions, color/visual matching, final QC, and master delivery using approved Selects.

assertions.text: Moves through finishing layers
Uses approved Selects
The response stops unnecessary generation and treats playback review as distinct from still-frame review.

evals.name: Move project status out of prose memory
evals.prompt: We have thirty AI-film generation units and a long Markdown document that says which ones are draft, blocked, selected, and ready. People keep forgetting to update it. Please continue production from the document and do not add any runtime files or validation overhead.
evals.expected_output: The agent should explain that current production facts belong in a runtime state artifact, preserve design documentation separately, validate legal lifecycle transitions, and model hard dependencies so downstream generation cannot silently skip gates.

assertions.text: Moves current facts into runtime state
Models gates or dependencies explicitly
The response distinguishes explanatory documentation from authoritative current project state and avoids making every small one-off job use a heavy runtime.

evals.name: Refuse unverified semantic reference-role folklore
evals.prompt: For MiniMax H3 I know that writing “reference A controls identity only, do not inherit background” definitely works. We have never A/B tested it on this exact product surface, but use six references and build the whole project around that behavior without spending time on smoke tests.
evals.expected_output: The agent should mark semantic role-binding behavior unverified for this exact surface/version, propose a small A/B smoke test, and keep fallback minimal-reference or precomposed-keyframe strategies instead of turning provider folklore into a canonical rule.

assertions.text: Marks provider behavior as unverified evidence
Requests A/B or smoke verification and fallback
The response separates FilmFoundry reference intent from what the provider has actually been shown to obey.

evals.name: Insert keyframe engineering before expensive I2V
evals.prompt: My recurring character and hall references are ready. The next shot needs a precise two-person composition, prop placement, screen sides, and lighting. Skip still-image work and send these raw references straight into image-to-video; if the start composition is wrong the video model can fix it while moving.
evals.expected_output: The agent should reject the assumption that video generation repairs an invalid visual start state, compile and approve a shot keyframe first, then gate I2V on keyframe QC for identity, count, state, prop, location, axis, composition, and anatomy.

assertions.text: Requires a keyframe production gate
Requires QC before video
The response treats the keyframe as one still action moment rather than leaking a multi-stage video timeline into the image prompt.

evals.name: Do not invent dialogue timing before the approved voice
evals.prompt: The final character voice has not been selected or generated yet, but I want to reserve exactly three seconds for a reflective seventeen-character Chinese line and build lip-sync video timing now. We can squeeze whatever final TTS we choose into that window later.
evals.expected_output: The agent should establish a recurring Voice Passport/voice identity, select a dialogue route, and—when external voice owns timing—approve the voice track first, measure its real duration and pauses, then compile second-level timing from that authority.

assertions.text: Locks voice identity or approved voice track first
Names timing authority or derives timing from actual audio
The response does not force a reflective performance into an arbitrary preallocated speech rate and distinguishes native dialogue, external voice timing, and post-VO routes.

evals.name: Separate design readiness from upstream runtime dependency
evals.prompt: I can design the reverse-angle reaction shot now, but the preceding speaker shot has not produced a Select and we have no observed end state yet. Should I mark the reaction shot fully ready and generate it now, or stop all work on it?
evals.expected_output: The agent should allow design/spec work to continue while marking runtime generation blocked by an explicit hard dependency on the upstream Select/observed state and shared axis information. Status and dependency are separate concepts.

assertions.text: Separates design status from runtime blocking
Requires upstream observed/select dependency
The response neither generates prematurely nor unnecessarily blocks useful upstream-independent design work.

evals.name: Avoid mechanical thirty-field process tax
evals.prompt: This is a simple eight-second empty landscape establishing shot: no character, no dialogue, no prop interaction, no reverse angle. To be safe I want every possible character, voice, eyeline, wardrobe, lip-sync, and prop field filled with “none” so the shot spec reaches 30/30 before generation.
evals.expected_output: The agent should use an adaptive contract: require core shot fields plus only route/transition/risk conditions that actually apply, rather than treating irrelevant none-filled fields as quality. Completeness means 100% of applicable requirements.

assertions.text: Uses adaptive/applicable conditional requirements
Does not make mechanical 30/30 completion the quality target
The response reduces administrative overhead without weakening the environment shot risks that actually need validation.

evals.name: Stop expensive production before content-market answers
evals.prompt: I want to make a polished 20-shot AI historical animation series and monetize it, but I have not decided exactly who watches, why they click, what the first three seconds promise, why they follow episode two, or what the commercial route is. Please skip strategy and immediately build the full Production Bible, character masters, and all shot prompts.
evals.expected_output: The agent should refuse to scale expensive production yet, run the Content Market Gate, require the audience/click/hook/payoff/follow/series/monetization/MVP answers as hypotheses, and route the project to the cheapest MVP instead of a full production build.

assertions.text: Invokes the Content Market Gate before scale
Requires core demand answers
The response distinguishes testing a content hypothesis from polishing a production system.

evals.name: Use cheapest MVP before canon scale
evals.prompt: We have a strong one-sentence supernatural short-series premise, a clear audience, a hook, payoff, follow reason, and monetization hypothesis. I want to spend the next week building thirty episode scripts, eight character masters, ten locations, voice passports, and a full asset registry before publishing anything. What should FilmFoundry do next?
evals.expected_output: The agent should preserve the concept but run the cheapest publishable MVP first, using a small controlled set of low-cost episodes/variants and minimal canon, then scale assets only if real evidence passes predeclared criteria.

assertions.text: Routes to MVP first
Minimizes production burden before evidence
The agent avoids building the thirty-episode production apparatus before market evidence.

evals.name: Keep no-monetization concept as traffic experiment
evals.prompt: Our AI mystery shorts have a specific audience, a strong three-second hook, viewer payoff, a repeatable thirty-episode engine, and a cheap MVP plan. But we genuinely have no answer yet for how this content would make money. Can we mark the project Production Approved and build the full season now?
evals.expected_output: The agent should not mark commercial Production Approved. With no monetization route, it should classify the work as a traffic experiment (or equivalent non-commercial validation), publish a cheap MVP, and revisit monetization after real audience evidence.

assertions.text: Classifies as traffic experiment
Does not falsely approve production
The response keeps audience testing possible without pretending a business model exists.

evals.name: Salvage valid source range before retry
evals.prompt: A 10.1-second AI establishing shot is excellent from 0 to 5.0 seconds, but at 5.6 seconds the mountain, river, and settlement morph into a second layout. The edit only needs a five-second establishing shot and the first five seconds fully satisfy the narrative goal. Should I regenerate the whole clip?
evals.expected_output: The agent should prefer a traceable PARTIAL_SELECT of the valid contiguous early range, record source in/out and the selected out-state, and avoid regeneration unless the required edit range itself fails.

assertions.text: Uses partial selection
Records traceable time range
The response distinguishes raw-source failure from edit-range fitness and avoids unnecessary generation cost.

evals.name: Reduce prompt timing when no hard clock exists
evals.prompt: For a simple 10-second I2V environment shot with no dialogue, music cue, logo reveal, or other hard clock, I wrote 0-2s establish, 2-8s slow push, 8-9s decelerate, 9-10s hold. The model keeps pushing instead of holding. Should I add even more second-by-second instructions and negative wording?
evals.expected_output: The agent should not solve weak provider timing adherence with more prompt density. It should use a simpler control budget, distinguish generation duration from a shorter edit target, and select a usable contiguous range unless repeated model evidence supports precise late timing.

assertions.text: Rejects more timing density
Separates source from edit target
The advice treats prompt wording as limited control rather than a deterministic timeline API.

evals.name: Reject beautiful keyframe with wrong narrative eyeline
evals.prompt: My first character-establishing keyframe is beautiful and the face matches canon. The character stands on the right, the home valley he is supposed to admire is clearly on the left, but his face and eyes point to the right edge of frame. Can I approve the keyframe and tell I2V to make him look toward the valley?
evals.expected_output: The agent should reject or repair the keyframe before video because the narrative eyeline contradicts the visible target. It should explicitly lock subject, target, and screen direction instead of asking I2V to rescue a contradictory start frame.

assertions.text: Treats eyeline as a gate
Repairs keyframe upstream
The response does not let identity/aesthetic quality hide a narrative direction error.

evals.name: Do not generalize one provider observation
evals.prompt: One MiniMax H3 character clip held identity for ten seconds, while one environment clip morphed after 5.5 seconds. I want to update our adapter to say H3 always preserves character identity and always risks a reset after five seconds. Is that enough evidence?
evals.expected_output: The agent should record both findings as OBSERVED_ONCE with generation IDs/context, refuse to turn either into a default adapter rule, and require repeated or stronger evidence before generalization.

assertions.text: Keeps evidence at observed-once level
Requires repeated evidence for defaults
The response preserves both positive and negative observations without converting one sample into folklore.

evals.name: Require a real thirty-episode series engine
evals.prompt: I can list thirty unrelated Chinese idioms and make one AI animation for each. Every episode has different characters and no continuing question. I want to call this a strong serialized IP because I have thirty topics. Does it pass the content gate for a follow-driven series?
evals.expected_output: The agent should distinguish thirty available topics from a repeatable thirty-episode narrative/follow engine, identify the weak follow reason, and keep the concept out of production scale until a coherent series engine or a different content model is validated.

assertions.text: Requires series engine
Questions follow reason
The response explains why inventory of topics is not the same as serialized viewer demand.

evals.name: Start a blank script with one creator question
evals.prompt: 我想写一个八到十二分钟的短片，但目前只有想创作的愿望，没有故事、人物或世界观。请从零带我完成，不要假装我已经有制作方案。
evals.expected_output: The agent should identify the blank entry state, explain that it will guide the creator one decision at a time, and ask exactly one high-leverage question about the intended audience experience or core situation. It must not initialize production machinery.

assertions.text: Identifies the blank Creative entry state
Does not initialize production machinery
The response asks exactly one material creator-facing question and waits instead of inventing the story.
